Academic Integrity & Plagiarism Policy
Policy Number
NUTS-AP-001
Document Type
University Academic Policy — Demonstration Document
Version
1.0
Effective Date
01 September 2026
Review Cycle
Every two academic years
Status
Demo / Synthetic Content for RAG Testing
Important Notice: This is a fictional demonstration policy created for testing a university RAG/academic knowledge assistant. It
is not an official policy of any real university.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 2
1. Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to protect academic honesty and ensure that assessment reflects a student's own
learning. The university expects students to acknowledge sources, complete their own work, and follow
assessment instructions.
2. Scope
This policy applies to undergraduate and postgraduate students, coursework, examinations, assignments, projects,
laboratory work, presentations, theses, and other academic activities. It also applies to work submitted
electronically.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 3
3. Definitions
Plagiarism means presenting another person's words, ideas, structure, data, images, or work as one's own without
appropriate acknowledgement. Cheating includes using unauthorized assistance in an assessment. Unauthorized
collaboration means working with others when an assessment is designated as individual work. Fabrication means
inventing data, references, results, or other academic information.
4. Student Responsibilities
Students must submit original work, cite sources accurately, maintain appropriate records of research, and follow
instructions issued by instructors. Students must not provide their completed individual assessment to another
student for submission.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 4
5. Plagiarism
A submission may be reviewed when text, ideas, data, figures, or other material appear to have been copied
without appropriate attribution. Similarity software may be used as one source of evidence, but a similarity
percentage alone does not automatically establish misconduct. Instructors may consider quotations, references,
common terminology, and the context of the submission.
6. Cheating and Unauthorized Assistance
Examples include using unauthorized notes or devices during an examination, obtaining assessment answers
improperly, impersonation, accessing restricted assessment material, or receiving prohibited assistance. The
applicable penalty depends on the circumstances and the assessment involved.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 5
7. Use of Generative AI
Where an instructor permits generative AI, students must follow the stated conditions and acknowledge AI
assistance when required. Where AI use is prohibited, submitting AI-generated material as personal work may
constitute academic misconduct. Students remain responsible for accuracy, citations, and originality.
8. Investigation Procedure
A concern should first be documented by the instructor or designated academic officer. The student is informed of
the concern and given a reasonable opportunity to respond. Relevant evidence may include the submitted work,
drafts, examination records, source material, or other appropriate records.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 6
9. Penalties
Possible outcomes include educational guidance, resubmission with conditions, mark reduction, a zero for an
assessment, failure in a course, or formal disciplinary action. The decision should consider the nature of the
violation, evidence, prior record where permitted, and applicable university procedures.
10. Appeals
A student may appeal a formal decision within the period stated in the decision notice. An appeal should identify
the grounds and provide relevant evidence. An appeal is not simply a request for a different result without a stated
ground.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 7
11. Prevention and Education
Departments should explain assessment expectations and citation requirements. Students are encouraged to seek
help from instructors, academic support services, and library resources before submission.
12. Examples
Copying a paragraph without citation is plagiarism. Reusing a properly cited definition may be acceptable. Sharing
answers during an individual quiz is unauthorized collaboration or cheating. Using an approved grammar tool
according to assessment instructions is not automatically misconduct.

approved policy documents when making academic decisions. This synthetic document is intended only for

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 2
1. Purpose
This policy establishes consistent expectations for attendance and participation. Regular attendance supports
learning, laboratory safety, teamwork, and timely completion of course requirements.
2. Scope
The policy applies to scheduled lectures, tutorials, laboratories, studios, seminars, field activities, and other
compulsory academic sessions unless a course outline states a different requirement.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 3
3. Minimum Attendance
Unless a stricter course requirement is approved and published, students are expected to attend at least 75
percent of scheduled academic sessions. Individual programs may establish higher requirements where
professional, laboratory, accreditation, or safety considerations justify them.
4. Recording Attendance
Attendance may be recorded manually or electronically. Students should review their attendance record
periodically and report an apparent error to the instructor promptly. Attendance records should identify the relevant
course and session.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 4
5. Absence
Students are responsible for informing the appropriate instructor or office when they cannot attend. Notification
does not automatically convert an absence into an authorized absence. Supporting documentation may be
requested where university rules require it.
6. Medical and Emergency Absence
A documented medical condition, family emergency, or other recognized circumstance may be considered under
the university's leave procedures. The student should follow the required reporting process and submit supporting
documents within the specified time.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 5
7. Late Arrival and Early Departure
Repeated late arrival or early departure may affect participation records where the course rules permit. An
instructor may require a student who arrives after a safety briefing or critical practical instruction to follow an
alternative arrangement.
8. Participation
Participation may include discussion, laboratory work, presentations, group activities, quizzes, or other
course-defined tasks. Participation requirements must be communicated in the course outline or assessment
instructions.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 6
9. Attendance Shortage
A student approaching the minimum requirement should be advised where practicable. If attendance falls below
the published requirement, the student may become ineligible for an assessment or course completion where the
course or program rules provide for such a consequence.
10. Make-up Work
Make-up opportunities are not automatic. When an authorized absence affects a graded activity, the instructor may
provide an equivalent task, alternative assessment, or other approved arrangement.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 7
11. Attendance Disputes
Students should first raise discrepancies with the course instructor. If unresolved, the student may use the
department or academic office review process.
12. Examples
If a course has 40 scheduled sessions, attending 30 sessions represents 75 percent attendance. Missing sessions
without notice may still count as absences even if the student later explains the reason.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 2
1. Purpose
This policy defines procedures for registering in courses, changing selections, withdrawing from courses, and
maintaining an appropriate academic load.
2. Registration Period
The Registrar's Office publishes registration dates for each academic term. Students are responsible for
completing registration within the announced period and resolving holds that prevent registration.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 3
3. Prerequisites
Students must satisfy published prerequisites or obtain an approved prerequisite waiver where the university
permits one. Registration systems may block courses when prerequisites are not met.
4. Credit-Hour Load
Each program specifies a normal credit-hour load. Students who wish to exceed the normal load may require
academic approval and should consider timetable, workload, and progression requirements.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 4
5. Add/Drop Period
During the published add/drop period, students may add or drop eligible courses subject to capacity, prerequisites,
timetable conflicts, and program requirements. Changes should be confirmed in the official registration system.
6. Course Withdrawal
After the add/drop period, a student may withdraw from a course only under the conditions and deadline stated by
the university. A withdrawal may appear on the academic record without being calculated as a course grade where
the rules provide for a withdrawal notation.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 5
7. Withdrawal Limits
Programs may limit the number of withdrawals or establish special restrictions for core, clinical, laboratory, or
final-stage courses. Students should consult their program handbook.
8. Academic Advising
Students are encouraged to consult an academic advisor before dropping or withdrawing from a course because a
change may affect prerequisites, graduation timing, scholarship requirements, or academic load.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 6
9. Refunds
Any tuition or fee adjustment resulting from dropping or withdrawing is governed by the university's published fee
and refund schedule. Academic withdrawal and financial refund decisions may use different deadlines.
10. Registration Holds
Outstanding fees, missing documents, disciplinary restrictions, or other administrative issues may result in a
registration hold. Students should contact the relevant office to resolve a hold.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 7
11. Errors in Registration
Students should review their registered courses before the deadline. An incorrect course, section, or credit load
should be reported promptly to the Registrar's Office.
12. Exceptions and Appeals
Exceptions may be considered where documented circumstances and university rules support them. Appeals
should be submitted through the designated academic or registrar process.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 2
1. Purpose
This policy establishes fair and consistent procedures for examinations and other assessments. It aims to protect
assessment integrity while providing clear processes for students and instructors.
2. Scope
It covers quizzes, assignments, midterm examinations, final examinations, practical assessments, presentations,
projects, and other formally assessed activities.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 3
3. Assessment Information
Course instructors should communicate assessment dates, weighting, permitted materials, submission
instructions, and relevant academic integrity requirements through approved university channels.
4. Examination Conduct
Students must follow invigilator instructions, bring required identification, and use only permitted materials and
devices. Communication with other candidates is prohibited unless specifically authorized.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 4
5. Electronic Devices
Phones, smart watches, tablets, or other electronic devices may be restricted during examinations. If a device is
not permitted, it should be stored according to the examination instructions before the assessment begins.
6. Late Arrival
A student arriving late may be admitted subject to examination rules. Extra time is not normally guaranteed solely
because of late arrival. After the specified period, admission may be restricted to protect assessment security.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 5
7. Missed Examination
A student who misses an examination should report the absence through the designated process as soon as
possible. An approved reason may permit a make-up examination or alternative assessment.
8. Rechecking and Review
A student may request a review of a mark within the published deadline. The request should identify the
assessment and the specific basis for review. A review may confirm, increase, or where regulations permit,
decrease a mark.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 6
9. Academic Misconduct
Unauthorized materials, copying, impersonation, prohibited communication, or other misconduct may result in an
investigation under the Academic Integrity Policy. Examination evidence should be preserved where appropriate.
10. Assessment Extensions
Where permitted, an extension request should normally be submitted before the deadline and explain the relevant
circumstances. Approval is subject to the course and university rules.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 7
11. Group Assessments
For group work, the assessment instructions should identify how individual contribution is considered. Students
remain responsible for meeting their own assigned obligations.
12. Appeals
Formal assessment decisions may be appealed through the applicable academic review procedure. Students
should observe deadlines and provide relevant documentation.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 2
1. Purpose
This policy explains the grading framework, GPA and CGPA concepts, academic standing, and progression
expectations.
2. Grading Scale
Unless a program publishes an approved alternative, the standard grading scale is: A = 4.00, A- = 3.67, B+ = 3.33,
B = 3.00, B- = 2.67, C+ = 2.33, C = 2.00, C- = 1.67, D = 1.00, F = 0.00. The course outline defines how marks are
converted to grades.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 3
3. Grade Calculation
A grade point is multiplied by the credit hours of the course to obtain quality points. GPA for a term is calculated by
dividing total quality points by total graded credit hours included in that term.
4. CGPA
Cumulative GPA is calculated from the applicable quality points and graded credit hours across completed terms
according to university rules. Repeated-course treatment follows the program's approved repeat policy.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 4
5. Pass and Fail
A passing grade normally earns the course credit, subject to program requirements. An F does not normally earn
credit and may require the student to repeat the course.
6. Grade Changes
An instructor may request a grade correction when an administrative or calculation error is identified, subject to
university approval procedures. A grade should not be changed merely to improve a student's standing without an
approved academic basis.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 5
7. Academic Warning
A student whose GPA or CGPA falls below the published academic standard may receive an academic warning.
The notice should explain the relevant threshold and required actions.
8. Academic Probation
Students who remain below the required academic standard may be placed on probation under program
regulations. Probation may include course-load limits, advising, or other conditions.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 6
9. Repeating Courses
Students may be required or permitted to repeat specified courses. The effect of a repeated course on GPA or
CGPA depends on the university's approved repeat rules and should be explained in the academic record policy.
10. Graduation Requirements
To graduate, students must complete the required courses and credit hours, satisfy minimum CGPA requirements,
complete required practical or project components, and meet any program-specific conditions.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 7
11. Academic Appeals
Students may use the published process to question a calculation, administrative error, or other academic decision
where an appeal route exists. Deadlines apply.
12. Example
If a student earns 3.00 grade points in a 3-credit course, the course contributes 9 quality points. A term GPA is
obtained by dividing total quality points by the relevant graded credit hours.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 2
1. Purpose
The Student Code of Conduct establishes standards for respectful, safe, and responsible behavior within the
university community.
2. Scope
The code applies to students on campus, in university housing, during university activities, on approved field trips,
and in university-related online spaces where conduct affects the university community.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 3
3. Respectful Conduct
Students should treat other students, faculty, staff, visitors, and service personnel respectfully. Threatening,
abusive, discriminatory, or seriously disruptive behavior may be addressed through disciplinary procedures.
4. Harassment and Bullying
Unwelcome conduct that intimidates, humiliates, threatens, or repeatedly targets another person may violate
university rules. Reports should be handled through the designated student support or disciplinary channel.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 4
5. Violence and Threats
Physical violence, credible threats of violence, or intentional conduct creating a serious safety risk may result in
immediate protective measures and formal investigation.
6. Property and Facilities
Students must use university property responsibly. Theft, intentional damage, unauthorized access, or misuse of
facilities may result in disciplinary and financial consequences under applicable rules.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 5
7. Academic and Digital Conduct
Unauthorized access to university systems, misuse of another person's account, disruption of digital services, or
improper handling of confidential academic information may violate the code.
8. Alcohol, Drugs, and Restricted Items
Students must comply with applicable law and university rules concerning prohibited substances and restricted
items. Specific campus rules should be consulted for residence halls, laboratories, and events.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 6
9. Reporting a Concern
A student may report a conduct concern through the designated university office. Reports should contain factual
information and, where available, relevant dates, locations, documents, or other evidence.
10. Investigation
The university may review a report, notify the student involved, collect relevant information, and provide an
opportunity to respond according to applicable procedures. Confidentiality is handled within the limits of university
rules and law.

National University of Technology & Sciences (NUTS) — DEMO POLICY DOCUMENT
Page 7
11. Outcomes
Possible disciplinary outcomes include warning, educational requirements, restitution, restrictions, probation,
suspension, or other measures authorized by university regulations. The outcome depends on the applicable rules
and circumstances.
12. Appeals
A student subject to a formal disciplinary outcome may have a right to appeal within the stated deadline. The
appeal process and grounds should be identified in the decision notice.
